camelback-echo-canyon.note: Echo Canyon Trail is open today but is subject to the City of Phoenix Trail Heat Safety Program mandatory closure from 8am to 5pm, since the NWS Extreme Heat Warning for the Phoenix metro area has been extended and remains active; this closure also applies to Cholla and Piestewa Peak Summit Trail for the full duration of the warning, now through Friday, August 28, 2026, 8pm MST. The National Weather Service confirms the Extreme Heat Warning is active, effective through Friday, August 28, 8pm MST, for afternoon highs of 111 to 113 degrees. Separately, Cholla Trail remains closed entirely August 17 through 28, 2026 for a sewer diversion project, so during that closure Camelback access is limited to Echo Canyon Trailhead outside the 8am to 5pm heat closure window. Echo Canyon Trail is also scheduled to close entirely September 2 through 18, 2026 for its own construction project. Hike before 8am or after 5pm and carry extra water. Source: City of Phoenix Parks and Recreation; National Weather Service.

A live NWS alerts check today found no active Extreme Heat Warning or Flood Watch for the Sedona area. Hike before 7am or after 7pm and carry extra water. fossil-springs.note: Heat safety advisory: this trail descends into a canyon with creek crossings. A parking permit ($6 per vehicle via Recreation.gov) is required through October 1, 2026; permits have been available seven days a week since May 2026. Permit holders must reach the FR 708/SR 260 junction by 2pm, and gates to the Dixon Lewis, Irving/Flume, Tonto Bench, Fossil Creek Bridge, and Homestead lots close at 3pm; camping remains prohibited. No Flood Watch was active for the Fossil Creek area per a live NWS alerts check today. Hike early morning and carry extra water. Source: Coconino National Forest; Recreation.gov; National Weather Service.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Heat safety advisory: the National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for Grand Canyon Country (below 4,000 feet), covering Phantom Ranch, expired yesterday evening and has not been renewed, per a live check of NWS Flagstaff/api.weather.gov alerts; Grand Canyon National Park continues to rate heat risk at Phantom Ranch as Major and urges visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm. South Kaibab Trail is fully sun-exposed with no water source below the trailhead; water is on at the South Kaibab Trailhead. Confirmed open today with no closures reported. Source: National Weather Service; National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Heat safety advisory: the National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for Grand Canyon Country (below 4,000 feet), covering Phantom Ranch, expired yesterday evening and has not been renewed, per a live check of NWS Flagstaff/api.weather.gov alerts; Grand Canyon National Park continues to rate heat risk at Phantom Ranch as Major and advises that day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1.5 miles from the upper trailhead. Water is on at the Bright Angel Trailhead, Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse, Three-Mile Resthouse, and Havasupai Gardens; water status can change suddenly due to waterline breaks, so check current conditions before descending. Confirmed open today with no closures reported. Source: National Weather Service; National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

rim-trail.note: No closures reported today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: North Kaibab Trail is open for the 2026 season, reopened May 15, 2026, to foot traffic only, with stock use suspended. The National Park Service advises increased caution near Supai Tunnel and the lower trail due to Dragon Bravo Fire burn scar hazards, including debris flows, rockfalls, and flash flooding with little to no warning even when storms are not visible overhead. No active NWS Flood Watch was confirmed for the area today; the underlying burn scar flash flood risk persists through the monsoon season regardless. Water is off at Supai Tunnel, but on at Cottonwood Campground and Manzanita Day Use Area; carry all water needed elsewhere on the corridor. Grand Canyon National Park rates heat risk at Phantom Ranch as Major; the NWS Extreme Heat Warning for Grand Canyon Country expired yesterday evening and has not been renewed, per a live check of NWS Flagstaff/api.weather.gov alerts. Source: National Weather Service; National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
